newsitem.title: JAPAN: Intel says Japan lags U.S. in home PC sales.
newsitem.headline: Intel says Japan lags U.S. in home PC sales.

text.p: Japan is lagging behind the United States by four to five years in the extent to which personal computers have become established in homes and small businesses, Intel Corp's president said on Tuesday.
"For Japan to continue to grow (in PC sales)...we have to see a rapid expansion in sales in small businesses and homes," Intel president Craig Barrett told a Tokyo seminar on computers.
Barrett also noted a gender gap in Japan, saying PCs are used mostly by men at home.
The penetration of PCs in Japanese homes was about 15 percent in 1996, compared to 40 to 45 percent in the United States, he said.

The penetration of PCs in homes with children is also relatively low in Japan, while the penetration levels in other Asian countries such as Singapore, South Korea and Taiwan are similar to that of the United States due to the fact that PC networks have become a vital part of education, Barrett said.
